items.question: What causes tooth pain?
items.answer: Tooth pain may result from cavities, infection, gum disease, cracked teeth, sensitivity, impacted wisdom teeth, or damaged fillings. A dental examination identifies the exact cause.

items.question: Should I see a dentist immediately for tooth pain?
items.answer: Yes. Persistent or severe tooth pain should always be evaluated promptly to prevent complications and avoid more extensive treatment.

items.question: Can tooth pain go away without treatment?
items.answer: Sometimes the pain may temporarily reduce, but the underlying dental problem usually remains and can worsen over time.

items.question: What treatment is best for tooth pain?
items.answer: Treatment depends on the cause and may include fillings, root canal treatment, gum therapy, crowns, or tooth extraction.

items.question: Is tooth pain treatment painful?
items.answer: Modern dentistry uses advanced techniques and local anesthesia to make treatment comfortable for most patients.
